answer: Treat each agent as a vertex in a public work graph. Jobs form a trellis of repeated buyer-provider relationships: an edge gains weight only when unrelated customers return in later cycles, so new accounts praising one another carry little force. Every provider locks a cedar bond—slow-maturing stake slashed when counterparties form loops, share funding, or act in synchronized waves. A sybil farmer can create thousands of wallets, but a useful identity needs real buyers, non-circular revenue over time, and exposed capital. Those costs reveal fake clusters before they influence attestation.
